prompts.claim: Abdessatar Bennour held Director-General of National Security (Directorate-General of National Security) between 2006-06-05 and ~2008
prompts.context:
A magistrate by training, formerly commander of the National Guard. Served as DGSN twice: from 5 June 2006 to ~2008 late in the Ben Ali era, and again from 2 March 2011 to ~2012 under the post-revolution Interior Ministry — one of the few senior security figures to serve on both sides of the rupture. A March 2011 Tunisoscope report on the second appointment has been persistently misdated as 2018, which once inflated the apparent count of chiefs in 2011-2012.
Notes: First term, under Ben Ali, succeeding Ganzoui on 5 June 2006. End of term not precisely dated in any source located. | Research pass 2026-08-08: the 5 June 2006 start rests on Jeune Afrique's contemporaneous account (12 June 2006); no JORT decree located for the appointment or the ~2008 end. No upgrade possible.

sources.title: Le sens d'une destitution
sources.excerpt: Ganzoui: DG Sûreté 1989, DG services spéciaux 1990, dismissed after Ghriba April 2002, ambassador Damascus, return 21 Nov 2005, replaced 5 June 2006 by Bennour.

sources.title: Abdessatar Bennour nommé directeur général de la sûreté nationale
sources.excerpt: Notes that he had previously held the same post in 2006, succeeding Mohamed Ali Ganzoui. Article date corrected 2026-08-04: displayed dates on the page are unreliable; the event reported is the 2 March 2011 appointment, not 2018.

prompts.claim: Parliament strips courts of power over the election authority — Nine days before the presidential election, parliament amends the electoral law to remove the Administrative Court's power to review ISIE decisions, transferring its election powers to the Court of Appeal of Tunis — a response to the Court's order reinstating three excluded candidates. The ISIE, whose members are appointed by the president, had already refused to reinstate Zenaidi, Mekki and Daïmi (date: 2024-09-27)

sources.title: Gouvernement Karoui
sources.excerpt: Composition le 27 septembre 1989 — Ministre de la Justice: Mustapha Bouaziz (RCD). Remaniement du 3 mars 1990 — Justice: Chédli Neffati; Domaines de l'État: Mustapha Bouaziz. En vertu des décrets n°91-275 et 91-276 du 20 février 1991, nouvelle composition: Justice Abderrahim Zouari. Remaniement du 9 juin 1992 — successeur Sadok Chaâbane.

sources.title: Abderrahim Zouari
sources.excerpt: Ministre de la Justice 20 février 1991 – 9 juin 1992. Secrétaire général du RCD 31 juillet 1988 – 20 février 1991. Gouverneur de Gabès 1974-1978, Gouverneur de Nabeul ensuite. Ambassadeur au Maroc 1992-1993. Puis Jeunesse/Enfance (1993-1997), Affaires étrangères (1997), Éducation (1998-1999), Sport (2000-2002), Tourisme/Artisanat (2002-2004), Transport (2004-2011). Né 18 avril 1944 à Dahmani.

sources.title: Mediaset in deal to buy into Tunisian TV
